what: OG-ap-11 pre-grade exercise of the DEPLOYED parser, run against the package bytes that are now live (CodeSha256 YeLmNn/Tkz+HYVVrCS/PeE+mISSAnH/8ilUUxPEnCmk=). Local, in-process; NO AWS call, NO sweep invoke, NO message planted. Its purpose is to de-risk the 12:10Z planting window: a malformed synthetic body parses to None, which LEAVES BOTH RECORDS ALONE and would fail AC2 for the payload's fault rather than the deploy's.
instrument: deployed schwab_runtime.dlq_message_family(), loaded by path from the package dir
what_this_DOES_establish: The deployed code reads requestContext.functionArn correctly and routes a correctly-shaped record to the right arm, and it fails CLOSED to leave-alone on five malformed shapes. So the path the condition-C question was about is now exercised END TO END through the live bytes.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: That AWS's REAL on-failure records carry that shape. This exercise uses bodies this seat authored, so it cannot evidence the real producer's shape -- that would be circular, which is exactly why a synthetic was refused as condition-C evidence. The real shape rests on the documented Lambda async on-failure destination contract plus OG-dq-1's corroborating read, and the real oracle remains AC2 on the scheduled 12:15Z sweep.

synthetic_body_shape.marked: synthetic: OG-ap-11 at the top level and inside requestPayload

planting_window: before ~12:10Z; the grade uses the SCHEDULED 12:15Z sweep, no ad-hoc invoke
queue_state_note: OG-dq-1 records a refill of 12 at 13:07Z daily and an unnamed consumer deleting the whole queue at about 16:00Z. 13:07Z is AFTER the 12:15Z sweep, so at grade time the queue should hold ONLY these two synthetics -- clean conditions, and the denominator is checkable at planting time.
